question: How many chromosomes are in a normal human cell made by meiosis?
explanation: Meiosis cuts the chromosome number in half, changing the standard 46 chromosomes down to 23 in each mature sex cell. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of crossing over during meiosis?

options.A: It stops cells from dividing too early
options.B: It speeds up cell division in the reproductive organs
options.C: It mixes up genes to create unique traits in offspring
options.D: It doubles the total number of chromosomes

explanation: During crossing over, sections of DNA swap between chromosome pairs, ensuring each sperm and egg carries a different mix of traits. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h1)

question: When do human females start forming their primary oocytes?

options.A: At the start of the first menstrual period
options.B: During fetal development in the womb
options.C: Only after a sperm enters the egg

explanation: A baby girl forms all her primary oocytes while growing inside her mother's uterus, long before she is born. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why does oogenesis involve an unequal division of cytoplasm?

options.A: To make sure polar bodies grow into backup eggs
options.B: To speed up the final stages of cell division
options.C: To provide the fertilized egg with enough stored food and nutrients
options.D: To balance the exact number of X and Y chromosomes

explanation: By packing most of the cytoplasm into one egg cell, the body ensures the early embryo has enough energy to survive its first few days. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h2)

question: Where does sperm production take place in the male body?
explanation: Sperm are produced inside the tiny, coiled tubes called seminiferous tubules located within the testes. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h3)

question: How is spermatogenesis different from oogenesis in its final outcome?

options.A: Spermatogenesis produces four equal-sized functional sperm cells
options.B: Spermatogenesis creates polar bodies that absorb nutrients
options.C: Spermatogenesis stops completely in middle age

explanation: While female cell division makes one large egg and tiny polar bodies, male cell division splits the cytoplasm evenly to make four working sperm. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT true about normal oogenesis?

options.A: Cells pause in development for many years
options.B: Continuous daily production of thousands of new eggs throughout life
options.C: Final division finishes only after fertilization
options.D: Unequal division of cytoplasm creates polar bodies

explanation: Unlike men who make sperm every day, women are born with a set number of eggs that gradually decrease over time. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is a sperm cell built so differently from an egg cell?

options.A: Eggs need tails to swim toward the sperm
options.B: Sperm need large amounts of cytoplasm to survive
options.C: Sperm contain multiple nuclei for cell fusion
options.D: Sperm are built for swimming, while eggs store nutrients for growth

explanation: A sperm sheds most of its cytoplasm to stay light and fast for travel, while an egg keeps its cytoplasm to feed the early embryo. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is the risk of chromosomal issues higher for older pregnant women?

options.A: Her eggs have been paused in development for decades and can fail to separate properly
options.B: Her ovaries make new germ cells rapidly
options.C: Her uterine lining lacks hormones for cell division
options.D: Her body produces excess polar bodies

explanation: Because a woman's eggs stay paused in early meiosis for many years, the cellular equipment can sometimes struggle to separate chromosomes correctly as she ages. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does ongoing sperm production relate to genetic changes over time?

options.A: Frequent cell division in older men can lead to copied mistakes or mutations
options.B: Spermatogenesis stops at age forty to prevent errors
options.C: Sperm cells are immune to genetic aging because they renew daily
options.D: Male cells pause in meiosis and cause high rates of Down syndrome

explanation: Because sperm-producing cells keep dividing throughout a man's life, the DNA is copied repeatedly, which can occasionally introduce small spelling mistakes over time. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h5)
